progress: Added measurement::Measurement typed Start/Value lifecycle, zero/add accumulator and to_f64 conversion. Suite::bench_measured registers a distinct batch-total metric and executes synchronous operations in BatchPolicy waves. A separate timer supplies wall observations and scheduling; custom numeric totals cannot replace elapsed time. Invalid finite/nonnegative conversion fails explicitly. Suite::bench_measured_with_input now prepares fresh inputs and deferred-output buffers before both clocks, excludes input destruction, and follows DropPolicy for outputs. Plain bench_measured shares this implementation via unit input. bench_measured_with_owned_input moves each fresh input exactly once using the same wave engine; consumed input destruction is included, while returned inputs follow output-drop policy. Ownership and lifecycle contracts distinguish this from borrowed inputs. bench_async_measured_with_input runs borrowing futures sequentially on a lazily initialized executor created before the custom wave timer. Future construction, polling and completion are included; outputs follow DropPolicy. Added bench_async_measured and bench_async_measured_with_owned_input using the shared async borrowed-input engine. Plain operations include output destruction; owned futures distinguish consumed input destruction from returned input deferred destruction. Added ValueFormatter with human/shared-scale, throughput and machine conversions. format_observations normalizes batches, uses one population-wide typical maximum, preserves missing rows, validates converted values/count/unit and leaves Run unchanged. Formatted rows serialize to JSON and render to Markdown/HTML tables. Suite::formatter registers presentation per case/metric; formatted_metrics checks the full metric contract on loaded runs. main emits human tables to console/HTML and human+machine formatted.json/BENCH_FORMATTED, retaining raw Run and comparison data. Loaded baselines are formatted with currently registered callbacks only when metric contracts agree. Suite main persists formatted snapshots in versioned provenance. Each snapshot hashes its metric contract and raw observations. report Markdown/HTML restores it without custom code; missing selected metrics are ignored and changed source values produce an explicit stale-formatting diagnostic. Snapshot writes validate before mutating the run. Registered formatters now receive fixed work counters automatically via scale_throughputs. Per-counter throughput rows preserve work_per_operation in JSON/snapshots and render in console/HTML; snapshot restore rejects changed work counters. New snapshot field has a serde default for prior saved runs. Primary html_run reports now include plots of saved human-formatted observations, grouped by display unit with separate process/variant series. Stale snapshots produce explicit unavailable diagnostics, and plot captions state thinning/missing-value behavior. Unified report HTML now renders saved human-unit observation plots; --no-plots retains tables only. Stale formatter snapshots suppress formatted graphs with explicit diagnostics while keeping the rest of the report usable. format_comparison validates compatible independent runs and selects a shared formatter scale over both normalized raw populations. comparison_chart labels baseline/candidate/process series; direct Cargo named-baseline HTML uses it with registered callbacks rather than overlaying independent snapshots. Dynamic input work now flows through Suite::formatted_metrics and ValueFormatter::scale_input_throughputs. Matching uses case/variant/process/sequence/pair and requires equal operation counts; default conversion requires one shared unit. Dynamic snapshots retain null work_per_operation and a separate hash of wall observations, preserving existing fixed-work snapshot encoding. ProcessFormatting validates worker snapshots before rebasing process/variant identities, intersects complete formatted metric/counter coverage across workers, and saves new hashes after raw observations are merged. Runner protocol invokes it, preserving per-row units and keeping differently scaled units on separate graphs. ValueFormatter now has optional format_value/format_throughput human-text overrides on scaled numeric values and units. Text is persisted in backward-compatible optional display fields and escaped in Markdown/HTML; machine and unavailable rows never invoke text callbacks. Numeric graph data remains separate. Added measurement/formatter attributes for sync/async functions, fresh borrowed/owned inputs, runtime arguments, batch/drop policies and input counters. Inline group defaults inherit both expressions. Unsupported threads/allocator combinations and formatter without measurement are compile errors; imported groups must declare these defaults locally. Saved formatter charts now include each fixed/dynamic throughput counter, grouped by display unit and process/variant. Named-baseline comparison_chart also formats both raw populations jointly for each throughput counter and plots them on a shared scale. Captions correctly point to run.json for complete persisted rows. Caller-defined typed custom totals now support sync/async and attributes with args and formatter. Lifecycle hooks are not invoked; the caller returns the complete batch total. Independent wall timing excludes lazy executor construction and numeric conversion. Direct Cargo now writes formatted.csv with machine rows, normalization metadata, exact integer identities and missing reasons. Saved-run export --format formatted-csv validates formatter snapshots, rejects missing/stale output and preserves original run bytes. Airbug machine callbacks receive normalized batch values; Criterion CSV callbacks receive sample totals, so Airbug labels this normalization explicitly and retains raw totals in its raw export. Added format_bootstrap_metric and Suite::formatted_bootstrap: absolute estimates, confidence endpoints, standard errors, min/max and retained draws use one shared scale across variants. Direct Cargo saves formatted-estimates.json/html with no-plots support, retaining raw estimates separately. Outlier points, quartiles and finite signed fences now share the same formatter call; classification labels, counts, indices and missing fences are preserved. Nonfinite output and reordered values are rejected. The bootstrap_formatter integration test verifies signed fences, shared units and immutable raw reports. Regression totals, slope estimates/intervals/errors and retained slope draws now share the same scale, preserving process identity, operation counts and R-squared. Statistical formatters must apply a positive linear conversion without offset; integration coverage checks regression fields and rejects offsets, nonlinear transforms, collapsed scales and infinity.

upstream_formatter_geometry_audit.contract: ValueFormatter::scale_values chooses a unit from typical_value, can be called repeatedly with the same typical value, and prohibits NaN. The trait documentation does not state monotonicity or linearity.
upstream_formatter_geometry_audit.regression_behavior: Both inspected backends transform observed totals and three values at max_iters (point slope and slope interval endpoints multiplied by max_iters). They connect transformed endpoint values to an untransformed origin. Plotters uses a straight line and triangular polygon. This is not a general transformation of a regression curve or confidence region.
upstream_formatter_geometry_audit.distribution_behavior: Plotters transforms original confidence endpoints and bootstrap draws separately; the transformed endpoints define the KDE interval. It does not calculate percentile bounds of transformed draws.
analytical_counterexamples: For f(y)=y^2, slope=2 and max_iters=3, the transformed line endpoint is 36. A straight line from the origin gives y=12 at x=1; transforming the original fit gives f(2)=4.
For f(y)=(y-4)^2 and original interval [2,6], both transformed endpoints are 4 while the image contains 0 at y=4. Endpoint-only bounds cannot represent this region.
upstream_formatter_geometry_audit.airbug_status: Monotone regression curves and confidence bands have explicit transformed coordinates. Nonmonotone statistical intervals use transformed bootstrap percentiles. Nonmonotone regression confidence bands remain unsupported; this audit does not close that gap.
upstream_formatter_geometry_audit.acceptance_boundary: Do not infer correct arbitrary nonlinear plotting from the permissive formatter trait or upstream endpoint plotting. Distinguish callable formatter domain, visual behavior and statistical interval interpretation in the final comparison.
